Thanks Karthik — quick product note from my side. Enforcing a strict US-only serving path with no cross-region fallback is possible, but there are trade-offs to document:

1) Model variants: Our hosted catalog typically falls back to compatible model variants (smaller size / lower perf) to preserve availability. A hard no-fallback policy means we either reserve capacity on the same variant or fail requests when the pool is saturated. That changes expected error rates under burst.

2) Dedicated pool vs Private: For this pilot we can either: (a) reserve a dedicated pool in our US region (economically heavier, predictable capacity), or (b) provision Private (VPC) deployment if MedIntegra requires full tenant isolation.

3) Latency/SLO: Forced selection of a specific variant may increase tail latency if that variant scales poorly at short sequence-length distributions. We should instrument a short synthetic test and report expected p95/p99 before the pilot.

4) Runtime controls: we can expose a "no_fallback" flag per route and a hard capacity threshold. Ops will need to supply the runbook for what happens when threshold is hit.

I attached a quick draft runbook and an allowlist template for IPs to get us started. Please treat the runbook as a working draft; Evelyn can iterate with ops specifics.

Attachments: prod-runbook-draft.pdf, allowed-ips.csv

Marcus

Karthik / Marcus — ops perspective and a sketch of the runbook steps. High level: this is operationally achievable for a limited pilot, but requires explicit capacity reservation and runbook acceptance by the customer. Key bullets: 

- Capacity reservation: ops needs a committed pool size for the pilot window. If MedIntegra cannot provide traffic estimates, we should propose a conservative reservation (e.g., 4x estimated avg QPS) and allow a one-time bump window.
- Hard no-fallback enforcement: implement a routing gate that checks region + route flag. If saturated, requests return a 503-like error with our pilot-specific error code and a link to the incident page.
- Incident runbook (draft):
  1) Detect saturation via token-queue metrics -> alert to on-call (pager)
  2) Runbook owner triages (Ops on-call) and notifies customer via CS (Grace)
  3) Short-term mitigation options: (a) enable temporary burst allowance from reserved burst capacity, (b) throttle non-critical endpoints for the pilot customer if there is shared infra, (c) coordinate a manual capacity bump (requires 24–72h lead time).
- Audit and evidence: we will produce request-level logs with region and route flags plus KV cache retention metadata. Security asked for two logs samples — we can produce those on request.
- On-call: Evelyn Hart (ops lead) primary during PST hours, backup Naomi Feldman (sec/compliance). Contact: +1-415-555-0112 and ops-oncall@redwood.ai
- Cost note: committed pool + burst buffer estimated at $8k–$12k/month for the pilot depending on reserved size.
